names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 9 aprilie, «Sfântul Mucenic Eupsihie din Cezareea Capadociei».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Ευψύχιος που μαρτύρησε στην Καισαρεία», with the rank word and the clause naming where he was martyred left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 9 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Св. муч. Евпсихије.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and with муч. left off as well, the rank word this source uses for a martyr, which this folder already carries in `types`. The heading leaves no epithet and names neither the city nor the reign, so the bare forename is all the source gives; it is the identical form, off an identical heading, that `eupsychius-of-caesarea-under-hadrian` carries for the Julian 7 September, and that fold is deliberate and recorded.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 9 aprilie — «Sfântul Mucenic Eupsihie din Cezareea Capadociei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Ευψύχιος που μαρτύρησε στην Καισαρεία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 9 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives no years at all: it sets him only «στα χρόνια του Ιουλιανού του Παραβάτη», in the years of Julian the Apostate, so no `dates` were taken. Its third couplet names the day — «Φάσγανον ἀμφ' ἐνάτην Εὐψυχίου ἔκταμε λαιμόν», the sword cut Eupsychius's neck about the ninth. The same site keeps a second Eupsychius of Caesarea, under Hadrian, whom the corpus holds separately with a Greek row on 7 Σεπτεμβρίου; this is the one under Julian, as both the day's line and the page's own narrative of the idol of Fortune show.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.04.2026 (9. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Евпсихије.“

attestations.note: The day's first of two entries, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek both keep him on. **This is the Eupsychius of Julian's reign and not the other one**: the entry sets him «у време цара Јулијана Оступника», names the idol Fortune, the wedding, the pulling down of the temple and the renaming of the city, and dates the death 362 — every mark of this folder and none of `eupsychius-of-caesarea-under-hadrian`, whom the corpus keeps on 7 September and who is already linked from this folder's life as a different man. **A death of 362 was added where this folder had none** — „посечен, 362. год.“, printed flat — and it is the only year any source read for this folder gives it: doxologia's life sets him in Julian's reign without a number and saint.gr does the same. `node .tmp/dd.mjs 362` reads in Russian and Greek. New besides that: that **not a single day of married life was given him**, the pagan feast falling at the time of his own wedding; that Julian's decree included **rebuilding the temple of Fortune at the Christians' own expense**; that he was **first bound to a tree and cruelly tortured** before the beheading, where doxologia has the rack and the iron combs — a variant recorded and not reconciled; and the **words** of the exchange with Basil, which this folder's life had only in summary: «You mock us, O emperor; we brought you bread, which we eat, and you give us cattle fodder, which you cannot by your own authority turn into food for men», and the emperor's «Know that I will feed you with that hay when I return from Persia!» — the apostate never came back alive from Persia, the entry closes, but perished there by a deserved and unnatural death. **The fold is deliberate**: the stored form Евпсихије is the same bare forename `eupsychius-of-caesarea-under-hadrian` holds, and the two Prologue headings are word for word identical — „Св. муч. Евпсихије.“ for the Julian 7 September and for the Julian 9 April alike — so this source offers no way to tell them apart at all. Recorded in the run's findings before this was committed. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the hymn on this folder is the Romanian calendar's.

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Eupsihie, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nestricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Eupsihie din Cezareea Capadociei», Glasul 4

english.text: Thy martyr Eupsychius, O Lord, in his struggle has won from Thee, our God, the crown of incorruption; for having Thy strength, he overthrew his tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At his prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Εὐψύχως ἤνυσας, δρόμον τὸν ἔνθεον, καὶ καταβέβληκας, ἐχθρὸν τὸν δόλιον, τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Σταυροῦ, παμμάκαρ ἐνδεδυμένος ὅθεν συνηρίθμησαι, τῶν Μαρτύρων ταὶς τάξεσι, δόξαν αἰωνίζουσαν, κεκτημένος Εὐψύχιε. Ἀλλὰ μὴ διαλείπῃς πρεσβεύων, σώσαι ἠμᾶς τοὺς σὲ τιμώντας.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ’, Τὴν ὡραιότητα, on the page of Άγιος Ευψύχιος που μαρτύρησε στην Καισαρεία. It is his own and names him.

english.text: With good courage thou didst finish the godly course and cast down the crafty enemy, being clothed, O all-blessed one, in the whole armour of the Cross; whence thou wast numbered with the ranks of the martyrs and hast gained everlasting glory, O Eupsychius. But cease not to intercede for the saving of us who honour thee.

hymns.text: Ὡς εὐσεβείας θεόδμητον ἄγαλμα, τῆς ἀσεβείας καθεῖλες τὸ ἳδρυμα, καὶ εὒψυχος ὤφθης πρὸς ἄθλησιν, ἐν εὐψυχίᾳ τμηθείς τὸν αὐχένα σου· διό σε ὑμνοῦμεν Εὐψύχιε.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τοῖς τῶν αἱμάτων σου, on the page of Άγιος Ευψύχιος που μαρτύρησε στην Καισαρεία. It is his own, names him, and turns on the idol he pulled down.

english.text: As a statue of piety built by God thou didst pull down the edifice of impiety, and wast shown of good courage for the contest, thy neck being cut through in good courage; therefore we hymn thee, O Eupsychius.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 9 April: „Св. Евписхије беше најпре везан за дрво и мучен љуто, а по том посечен, 362. год.“ — first bound to a tree and cruelly tortured, and then beheaded, in the year 362. The year is printed flat and not as «about». It is the only year any source read for this folder gives: doxologia.ro's life sets the martyrdom in the reign of Julian the Apostate without a number and saint.gr does the same, and 362 falls inside that reign. `node .tmp/dd.mjs 362` reads in Russian and Greek.
